brief.scope: Independently review only test_agy_dispatch.py and agy_dispatch_support.py against declared worker contract and original native inputs. No production bodies. Check actual black-box command effects, one NDJSON stdin turn, session/cwd ownership, resume or declared refusal, usage without double-counting and live supervision. Identify invented seams, setup/import errors, unconditional refusals mistaken for positive controls or native wire inventions. Later permission evidence is supplied separately to assess fixture compatibility; do not demand runtime discovery proof from synthetic tests. Run focused discovery/lint and full-range whitespace for these files. No new matrix, edits, vendors, credentials or full floor. Return stamped acceptance verdict inline.

findings.claim: Both live-supervision cases pass --cap-out on the launch verb, which launch.py's _launch_parser does not define (--cap-out exists only on the resume subparser, launch.py:2180 vs 2196-2211). Measured at e3d32ee the dispatch never happens: exit 2 with 'launch.py: error: unrecognized arguments: --cap-out 50'. Neither test can go green from any agy adapter work, so the brief's live wall/output supervision aim is unpinned; the fresh-launch cap comes from wires.budget(role) at launch.py:1299 and cannot be 50.
findings.reproduce: python3 -m unittest discover -s ops/devlane/dispatch/tests -p test_agy_dispatch.py -k AgyLiveStdoutSupervision -v

findings.claim: _spend_from calls _spend(job_dir, 'agy', session) but the landed seam is _spend(rec, stream, job_dir) (launch.py:1498) whose first statement is rec['harness']['name']; a PosixPath is not subscriptable, so the call raises TypeError inside call_seam and is swallowed to None (observed payload None in all three AgyTerminalUsage failures). The argument order is invented: satisfying it requires breaking the two existing callers at launch.py:1320 and launch.py:1906. The plant is also mis-aimed — raw.out is written, but _spend reads the harness store, and the session['stream'] path handed in is never created.
findings.reproduce: python3 -m unittest discover -s ops/devlane/dispatch/tests -p test_agy_dispatch.py -k AgyTerminalUsage -v; sed -n '1498,1503p' ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py; grep -n '_spend(' ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py

findings.claim: The negative control for 'unavailable live output evidence' is contaminated: AGY_FAKE_OMIT_USAGE only removes result['usage'] (line 137), while the step_update frame still carries usage with output_tokens=500 (lines 117-126), over the cap of 50. A launcher reading step_update usage sees over-cap output in the fixture that claims to have none. Separately, step_update.usage is not evidenced anywhere in the three supplied observation records — they report only result.usage (host 20260908T071244Z, stdin 20260908T073056Z, permissions 20260908T074530Z) — so this is an invented native field, against the file's own docstring at line 6 and the producer brief.

test_an_agy_read_job_is_not_the_write_role_refusal is the producer's declared single green, but it is an unconditional-refusal artifact, not a positive control. At e3d32ee every agy dispatch is refused 'worker: expected an implemented worker adapter; found agy', whose text simply lacks the string 'write-role-unadmitted'. The test would pass identically with agy removed from WORKER_HARNESSES, with no executable installed, or with no adapter at all; it certifies nothing about read admission.
findings.reproduce: python3 -m unittest discover -s ops/devlane/dispatch/tests -p test_agy_dispatch.py -k AgyWriteRoleUnadmitted -v

findings.claim: The tests pin the measured transport (--print= with --input-format stream-json, assertNotIn('--print', argv)) while CONTRACT.md at this same head still declares the bounded candidate transport as [executable, *isolation_flags, '--print', '--model', model, '--input-format', 'text', '--output-format', 'stream-json', '--disable-slash-commands']. The change lands the tests without reconciling the contract row, so a contract-conforming implementation fails these tests and a test-conforming one violates the declared row. The measured evidence backs the tests (bare --print consumed the next token, exit 2; --print= with --input-format text exited 1 empty prompt), which makes the contract row the stale half.

test_resume_terminal_usage_is_not_the_sum_of_both_process_totals never resumes. It calls _spend_from twice over the same ad-hoc directory with two independent raw.out writes; no record, no attempt chain and no accumulation path is exercised, so an implementation that did add a resumed cumulative total to a prior attempt total would still pass. The named aim (terminal usage without double-counting a resumed total) is unpinned even after the p1 signature defect is fixed.

The class is named for session/snapshot association but no assertion touches the snapshot, cwd or ref. call_stream is handed snap and self.ref (lines 301-304) and the return is only checked for path/ran/stream_id; the declared fourth element mismatch (CONTRACT.md: 'Preserve (path, ran, stream_id, mismatch)') is never read, and there is no case for a transcript recorded under a foreign cwd/ref, two concurrent sessions, or relocation — all named in the same contract row. The permissions record measured init.cwd against subprocess cwd with divergences [], so cwd ownership was measurable and is left untested.

call_seam's blanket 'except Exception: return None' erases the difference between 'the seam is absent' and 'the seam ran and crashed', against docs/wire.md absence discipline. Measured: _harness_meta('agy', ...) raises KeyError from the sandbox table at launch.py:391, and the test reports only 'None is not an instance of <class dict>'. The test's own guard at test_agy_dispatch.py:263-269, which would have named the exception, is dead code because call_seam already consumed it.
findings.reproduce: python3 -m unittest discover -s ops/devlane/dispatch/tests -p test_agy_dispatch.py -k test_harness_meta_uses_the_measured_store -v; sed -n '389,392p' ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py

findings.claim: The process-liveness check after the live cap-out is unreachable. install_live_child replaces the fake CLI with LIVE_CHILD, which writes only the AGY_FAKE_START marker; self.start_witness is written by _FAKE_CLI alone (launch_support.py:195-214), so 'if self.start_witness.is_file()' is always false and the pid_is_alive assertion never runs. Only the done-marker check carries weight.

test_resume_without_a_store_is_a_declared_refusal accepts either 'resume-store' or 'unsupported-capability', though CONTRACT.md names resume-store for exactly this case ('a home-isolated resume (including agy) has no session store'). It also plants only harness.name and session onto a record minted for grok, leaving grok's recorded isolation and executable in place, so a contract-conforming resume that rechecks 'the recorded executable against current worker selection' would refuse with class worker or executable and fail the test for a correct reason.

Six of the twenty-four cases assert on the private _argv/_effort_argv return value rather than on the argv the child actually receives. Only test_prompt_travels_as_one_user_ndjson_on_stdin reads the witness argv. Resume (--conversation), effort forwarding and permission-flag absence are therefore never confirmed as black-box command effects: a launcher could compute the asserted argv and spawn something else and still pass.

envelope.note: Reviewed only test_agy_dispatch.py and agy_dispatch_support.py as landed in 3432b5c..e3d32ee, against ops/devlane/dispatch/CONTRACT.md, ops/devlane/harness/isolation.py's agy entry, and the four supplied in/ records read whole. No production bodies were reviewed; launch.py was consulted only for seam signatures and the three lines needed to name a measured failure cause (_spend:1498-1503, _harness_meta:391, _launch_parser:2196-2211, _argv:506-509). No edits, no new matrix, no vendors, no credentials, no full floor. Verdict is changes on two p1 defects that make named aims of this brief unpinnable: the live-supervision pair dies in argparse before any dispatch, and the terminal-usage trio calls _spend with a fabricated argument order whose crash is swallowed by call_seam. What is well made and should survive: the transport, auth-leaf and store-path constants are traceable to the measured records rather than guessed; the synthetic usage numbers correctly model the native total (input+output, excluding thinking and cache — matching host 5518+123=5641 and stdin 11618+997=12615) and are chosen so a folded or doubled total cannot coincide with the terminal figure; the Claude-fallback decoy in the stream test targets the real else-branch at launch.py:599; and the fixtures stay compatible with the later permission evidence. Twenty-one red cases will land on a glob-discovering floor (ops/bin/suites.sh:21) until the adapter exists; that is this lane's declared red-first order, not a finding, but it is worth stating in the PR so the floor's colour is not read as a regression.
